title: OutlierCIM: Outlier-Aware Digital CIM-Based LLM Accelerator with Hybrid-Strategy Quantization and Unified FP-INT Computation
problem: Activation outliers in LLMs (rare large-magnitude values) introduce quantization challenges that degrade model accuracy and efficiency when accelerated in low-bit-width CIM arrays; existing outlier-aware methods struggle to balance accuracy and hardware efficiency.
motivation: LLM inference requires low-latency, energy-efficient acceleration; outliers force retention of high precision for small value fractions, wasting compute-in-memory (CIM) storage and incurring high latency.
method: OutlierCIM tackles three core problems. First, it groups outliers together (outlier-clustered tiling) to keep memory access and compute load balanced in the CIM array. Second, it uses flexible bit allocation (hybrid-strategy quantization with reconfigurable double-bit CIM macro arrays) so the hardware stores both normal values and outliers efficiently without wasting space or adding delays. Third, it adds a dedicated quantizer and post-processing step that unifies floating-point and integer arithmetic, since outlier handling requires both.
key_novelty: It's the first approach that designs the algorithm and hardware together specifically to handle activation outliers in CIM accelerators using hybrid quantization and reconfigurable storage.
contributions: Outlier-clustered tiling strategy to reduce inefficient memory access and workloads
Hybrid-strategy quantization with reconfigurable double-bit CIM macro arrays
Unified FP-INT computation path with dedicated quantizer for outlier-aware operations
4.54× energy efficiency and 3.91× speedup vs state-of-the-art outlier-aware accelerators
limitations: Evaluation on benchmarks not specified; generalization to other quantization strategies and workloads not discussed.
